CMS Medicare Part D Quarterly 2025 (Q1 to Q4), dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15, Rexulti (brexpiprazole): $1,127,195,022.03 over 121,062 beneficiaries = $9,310.89 per beneficiary (828,931 claims, $1,359.82 a claim). Not annualised. Rexulti is chosen because its label is the same one seltorexant seeks: an add-on to an antidepressant after inadequate response. Seltorexant's head-to-head comparator, quetiapine XR, is from the same augmentation class. Against the choice: Rexulti's Medicare beneficiaries include schizophrenia and Alzheimer's agitation patients. Its 6.85 claims per beneficiary is close to Trintellix's 6.54 (mature, MDD only). 2025 alternatives per beneficiary: Caplyta $9,788.05, Vraylar $10,176.39, Auvelity $5,461.14 (the novel oral MDD mechanism), Trintellix $4,080.30. The orexin class sells for far less in insomnia: Belsomra $2,094.23, Quviviq $2,203.43, Dayvigo $1,527.59. If payers treat seltorexant as a sleep drug, the price falls about 4.5x.

column11: Gain EP et al., IJERPH 2024;21(9):1209. Medicare Current Beneficiary Survey 2015 to 2019: 1,084 community-dwelling adults aged 65 or over with depression newly starting a serotonergic antidepressant. 30% were still on treatment at 181 days or more, so at a constant rate 1 - 0.30^2 = 0.91 a year. That is the book's convention on dazukibart, which annualises a six-month figure. The study is Medicare-based, like the per-beneficiary price. Corroboration: Olfson M et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:101-108 (MEPS 1996 to 2001) found 42.4% stopped within 30 days and only 27.6% continued past 90 days. The rate is a starting cohort's, applied to the whole stock, which overstates attrition for patients who stay on maintenance. The same 0.91 is used inside the anchor, so the anchor and the forecast move together.

Second, 53% respond inadequately to the first SSRI: STAR*D level 1 citalopram response was 47% (Trivedi MH et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40, doi 10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28). Third, about 60% of MDD patients have clinically relevant insomnia symptoms despite an SSRI or SNRI. That figure is J&J's own, from its press release of 2026-05-11, not an independent study. This 19.4% of MDD is the adjunctive-with-insomnia share the audit asked for.

Net price per beneficiary is $2,730.57 (its 2025 Part D $5,461.14, halved), and the pool is its whole label, 21,414,000. Stock: 47,646, 106,718 and 185,712. Carried forward at 9% (discontinuation 0.91): 0, 4,288 and 9,605. New starts: 47,646, 102,430 and 176,108. Capture rates: 0.2225%, 0.4794% and 0.8282% (2025, over an untreated pool of 21,263,925). The 2025 rate is the anchor because it is the last full year with a single label. The Q2 2026 run-rate ($180.3mm times 4) gives 1.1732%, but Auvelity added Alzheimer's agitation in June 2026. The anchor at the alternative discontinuation of 0.70 is 0.7225%. MULTIPLE 0.75x, A JUDGEMENT: 0.8282% x 0.75 = 0.6212% of seltorexant's own untreated label pool. For a higher multiple: the label pool is narrow and every patient in it is actively changing therapy; J&J has psychiatry sales scale; residual insomnia is common, and against quetiapine XR seltorexant showed four times less somnolence and less weight gain. Against: only one of two placebo-controlled Phase 3s was positive (a 2.6-point MADRS gain); it was not significantly better than generic quetiapine XR; and it enters a crowded add-on class of Rexulti, Vraylar, generic aripiprazole and quetiapine, and J&J's own Caplyta. Caplyta took the adjunctive MDD label on 2025-11-06 with 4.9 and 4.5 points against placebo, so J&J may put Caplyta first. At 1.0x the peak is 0.8282%.
